newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bank workers call off planned strike.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bank workers call off planned strike.

text.p: Israel's 35,000 bank workers on Monday called off plans to start an open-ended strike on Tuesday after a labour court ordered more talks on their demand for a five-day work week, a trade union official said.

"We expect the talks might untie a nine-year-old knot and that we will finally move to a five-day week," said Zion Shema of the Histadrut labour federation. "The (bank) workers' committees have decided not to strike on Tuesday."

He told Reuters the court had decided the head of Israel's anti-trust authority, the Bank of Israel's supervisor of banks, commercial bank officials and labour leaders would meet on Tuesday to try to break the impasse.
A ruling by anti-trust authorities that banks could not collectively agree to close branches on Fridays has held up a move to a shorter work week.

Workers at Israel's major banks have been striking for the past three Fridays and had planned an open-ended strike for Tuesday. They faced a restraining order from the court if they had resumed their work action tomorrow.
Israeli banks operate Sunday through Thursday and for a half day on Friday. During strikes on the last three Fridays, only banks at border crossings have remained open.
